title.narrative: Integrated Lifesaving Response to Malnutrition and Public Health Needs through Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Agriculture Support for Conflict-Affected peoples in West Belesa and Kinfaz Begela, woredas

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project titled “Integrated Lifesaving Response to Malnutrition and Public Health Needs in West Belesa and Kinfaz Begela,” is submitted by FIA, a women-led national NGO with an established operational presence and technical capacity in the target areas. The action will be implemented in partnership with Concern Worldwide (CWW), an international NGO acting as sub-implementing partner. This multisectoral humanitarian response aligns with the EHF 2025 First Standard Allocation under Thematic Priority 1, addressing acute malnutrition and gaps in essential services in conflict-affected, hard-to-reach areas. The proposed project has a budget of USD 1, Million and a 12-month implementation period. It aims to directly assist over 68,007 individuals across four sectors: Health (30%) and WASH (25%) by FIA, and Nutrition (20%) and Agriculture (25%) by CWW, with an estimated 100,000 indirect beneficiaries in Central Gondar Zone. The intervention addresses urgent needs resulting from conflict, displacement, and systemic service breakdowns that have compromised access to healthcare, safe water, nutrition, and livelihoods. The targeted woredas are identified as EHF priority locations due to alarming rates of malnutrition, food insecurity, and deteriorating health outcomes. FIA will deploy Mobile Nutrition and Health Teams (MNHTs) to provide integrated primary healthcare, maternal and newborn care, immunization, and reproductive health services through the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP). The health response includes community-level disease surveillance and risk communication to enhance early detection and prevention. The WASH component focuses on restoring essential services by rehabilitating non-functional water schemes, constructing gender-sensitive sanitation facilities near high-malnutrition areas, and distributing hygiene kits and water treatment chemicals to the most vulnerable households. Targeted hygiene promotion and behavioral change and communication (BCC) will engage caregivers and women-headed households to reduce disease risks. Concern Worldwide will implement Nutrition and Agriculture interventions using national protocols and global best practices. Nutrition activities include management of SAM/MAM, assessments, IYCF-E, cooking demonstration, community screenings, and commodity distribution tracking. The Agriculture component aims to restore livelihoods through the provision of climate-resilient seeds, tools, small livestock, and veterinary services, targeting food-insecure households. These efforts aim to build community resilience and reduce long-term dependency on aid. All components will integrate cross-cutting protection measures, including GBV risk mitigation, inclusion of persons with disabilities and older persons, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP). Women and girls will participate throughout the project cycle to ensure safe, inclusive, and responsive programming. Feedback and complaints mechanisms will be accessible, confidential, and culturally appropriate. The nutrition strategy emphasizes early identification and treatment of malnutrition among children under five and pregnant/lactating women (PLW) through mass screenings and awareness-raising. Strengthening local health systems and referral pathways will improve treatment capacity for SAM and MAM cases. Health workers (HWs), Health Extension Workers (HEWs), and the Health Development Army (HDA) will receive support to promote key maternal, infant, and young child feeding (MIYCF) practices through social and behavior change (SBC) interventions. This cost-effective, evidence-based action is aligned with Cluster cost-per-beneficiary benchmarks. FIA’s leadership ensures localization, sustainability, and accountability, delivering timely, principled, and community-centered humanitarian assistance to those most affected by crisis and exclusion.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
